# Rōmy

> Rōmy helps small nonprofits find new major donors at a fraction of the cost of existing solutions.

Rōmy is a donor intelligence platform built for small nonprofit teams. It uses AI-powered prospect research to surface wealth indicators, giving histories, and affinity signals — then distills them into actionable donor profiles.

## Features

- Donor Discovery: AI-powered prospect research with wealth indicators, giving history, and affinity signals
- Fraction of the Cost: No enterprise contracts or per-seat licensing — donor intelligence at a price built for small nonprofits
- Ready to Act On: Every prospect comes with connection points, giving capacity, and outreach angles

Somewhere on the second floor of a converted railroad depot on West Superior Street in Duluth, ninety-one miles down the North Shore, on the same morning at nine-forty-four, the record for G. R. Halstad in the CRM of the Second Harvest Northern Lakes Food Bank reads *sustaining $30/month by ACH since 8/2004, non-metro, non-alumnus, tier 5, mail-only, do not upgrade.* A short letter, with a great deal of tenderness, on the man in the third booth on a Friday morning in Itasca County — and on the six hundred and forty acres of virgin white pine north of Marcell that your CRM has been quietly, patiently, without any malice at all, failing to see.

- [The Ninth Card](https://getromy.app/blog/the-ninth-card): On the second Sunday of Advent, at a cherry-wood kitchen table in a small white clapboard house two blocks from the harbor on Petoskey Avenue in Charlevoix, Michigan, an eighty-four-year-old widow named Ruth Ellen Vanderberg lays out nine Christmas cards in a semicircle and prepares to write them for the last time. She has written nine every December, in the same careful cursive, with the same green Waterman fountain pen her husband gave her in the December of 1992, since a snowy Sunday in the December of 1994. Inside each: a folded check for one hundred dollars. Nine ledgers, in nine offices, in nine different towns, hold her as a small annual donor. None of the nine of them knows about the other eight, and none of them knows she is about to become — for whichever one of them thanked her, last spring, like she was a person — a two-thousand-dollar-a-year woman for the twenty years she has left. A short letter, with a great deal of tenderness, on the donor who is not lapsed, not low-value, not tier five; and on the small warm moment your fundraising software will only see once.

- [Capacity Scores Are the Astrology of Fundraising](https://getromy.app/blog/capacity-scores-are-the-astrology-of-fundraising): A capacity score is a four-digit number that promises — with quiet algorithmic confidence — to tell you what a stranger will give you over the next ten years. It is the most expensive horoscope in fundraising. A short letter on the donors the model misses, the donors the model misreads, and what to do with the dashboard the morning after you stop trusting it.
- [The Tuesday the Money Landed](https://getromy.app/blog/the-tuesday-the-money-landed): Somewhere today, in a parking lot in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday, a founder is staring at a wire confirmation on her phone — and her entire philanthropic life is about to begin. - [The Spouse You've Never Met](https://getromy.app/blog/the-spouse-youve-never-met): Every major gift is decided twice — once at your lunch, and once that night at a kitchen table you've never been to, between two people, one of whom you have never laid eyes on. A short letter on the second vote you don't get to attend, the partner you've been treating as a footnote, and why the most important person in your campaign may be the one who never answered your calls because, in three years, you never thought to make one.
- [Nine Years on Autopay](https://getromy.app/blog/nine-years-on-autopay): Your most loyal donor is almost certainly someone you've never called. She set up thirty dollars a month, meant every cent of it, and got filed under do-not-disturb the day the first charge cleared. A short letter on the quietest gift in your file — the standing yes nobody thinks to thank — and why the tool that finally makes giving effortless also made being forgotten effortless.
- [The Introduction Is the Gift](https://getromy.app/blog/the-introduction-is-the-gift): You spend months cold-cultivating a stranger while the person who could open that door is sitting at table six, eating the chicken, waiting to be asked. - [The Donor Nobody Owns](https://getromy.app/blog/the-donor-nobody-owns): Too big for the mail machine, too small for the major-gifts officer — your mid-level donors are the people your file was built to overlook. A short letter on the missing middle, and the donors quietly waiting to be claimed.
- [The First Gift Is a Question](https://getromy.app/blog/the-first-gift-is-a-question): Roughly four out of five first-time donors never give a second time. We call that a retention problem. It's really a manners problem. A short letter on the bravest gift a person ever makes — the first one, given on the least information — and the welcome it almost never gets.
- [On Asking Too Little](https://getromy.app/blog/on-asking-too-little): We brace for the no and never learn to be suspicious of the yes that comes too fast. - [The Room Was the Point](https://getromy.app/blog/the-room-was-the-point): The morning after the gala, the math looks like a verdict: a year of work, a netted-out spreadsheet, and the quiet feeling you failed.
